newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Tuesday in quiet trading as investors focused on the stock market, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.07 pct to 100.75
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.07 pct to 100.49.
Volume was moderate at 141 million shekels, with trading in Makams falling sharply to only 30 million shekels.
"The market is very stable and quiet. Investors are now showing more interest in the stock market," said Ari Eidelheit of Zeler Eblagon Securities.

"Bond prices are continuing to rise because investors are predicting that 1997 inflation will decline to 9.5-10 percent and that the Bank of Israel will lower its short-term rates," said Shlomit Ecker of Israel Discount Bank.
She said the central bank might even lower its base rate by 0.5 percentage points later this month from the current 14.7 percent.
Traders said CPI-linked bonds rose mildly on demand of 120 million shekels against supply of only 36 million shekels.

Traders noted that there were almost no sellers in the market. Unlinked bonds continued to rise today on demand of 170 million shekels against supply of only 11.5 million shekels. For Makams supply fell to only 6.0 million shekels.

Traders said dollar-linked bonds declined mildly following the rise of the shekel against the dollar. On Tuesday the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2440 shekels against 3.2470 on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
